passage: Ishita here, from flat 4A. When Aditi moved into 4B, I barely noticed. Then she kept "happening" to be at the lift at eight. First there was only a nod. Next she asked where the laundry was. A few days later she carried my parcel up from the gate and set it at my door, hovering a second too long before a small smile. She looked nervous each time, but she kept coming back. On Friday she asked if I wanted to share an auto to the market, and I said yes. Honestly, I would never have knocked on her door myself; I'd have waited for the awkwardness to pass. I can't be sure what she felt, maybe she was only being polite, but now we have a market plan for Sunday.

qa.q: What did Aditi carry up for Ishita?
qa.a: Aditi carried Ishita's parcel up from the gate.

qa.q: What might Aditi have been feeling as she hovered at Ishita's door?
qa.a: Aditi was probably nervous and hopeful, since Ishita noticed the hovering and the small smile, though Ishita admits she cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Aditi try next after the shared auto ride?
qa.a: Aditi could keep the small, repeated contact going, such as a chat at the lift or an invitation for tea, so the friendship keeps growing.

qa.q: Why might Ishita not have started the friendship herself?
qa.a: Ishita says she would never have knocked, so she may also fear awkwardness, and Aditi's small steps made it easy to say yes.

grounding: Aditi reaches out to a neighbour through small repeated contact instead of waiting to be invited.
